headline: Inferring unmeasured spatial omics layers from histology, transcripts and host signals
label: Cross Modal Spatial Omics Inference
summary: New preprints predict proteins, pathogens and transcriptomes from other spatial modalities, and one benchmarks cross-slice protein imputation directly.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring an unmeasured spatial layer from a measured one. TSNR predicts spatial protein abundance from spatial transcriptomics using protein-specific center signals, compact broad molecular context and a Huber loss. A separate benchmark of cross-slice imputation in spatial single-cell proteomics reports that learning-based methods outperform alignment-based ones. PatHoST uses weak supervision to reconstruct pathogen spatial distributions from host spatial transcriptomes, benchmarked on M. abscessus. On the histology side, a multi-scale graph neural network predicts bulk, spatial and single-cell transcriptomics from whole-slide images. HistoTx instead early-fuses H&E patches with transcript tokens at arbitrary resolution under self-supervised training. These two are described mainly through architecture rather than recovery testing. A secondary strand targets cancer survival modeling: CMVAE learns contrastive single-omic latents, GOTSurv applies unbalanced optimal transport to TCGA cross-sectional data, and DMG-PoE handles missing modalities with product-of-experts fusion. What is new is the explicit evaluation of whether imputed spatial layers are faithfully recovered.
